page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ce4.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel Xeon 8369HB cores operating at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per core ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates average performance across most compute and memory metrics. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests fall within the middle 50% tier, as do Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores. However, memory performance shows a notable bottleneck; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 465.3 GB/sec, uncached large-block read bandwidth drops to a weak 37.76 GB/sec, and the overall Passmark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25%. Database operations and physics simulations also register in the weak performance tier.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio, the instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-speed local storage or intensive database transaction rates. It is suitable for static web serving, Redis caching operations, and light text or image processing. It is not recommended for large-scale database operations or medium-to-large language model inference due to poor performance in those specific areas.
